standard_prerequisites.name: Flatness at a prime of the source can be detected after a flat base change to a prime of the target
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-base-change-flat-up-down}, cited at proof lines 4287-4289
standard_prerequisites.use: Carries flatness from the localised base change back to the localisation of the source.

standard_prerequisites.name: The induced map on closed sets is surjective, so every prime in the relevant locus of the source has a prime of the target above it
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: assumption (1) of the lemma, used at proof lines 4275-4277
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the prime of the target and the flat local map needed for the chase.

core_obligations: Choose a prime of the source lying over the relevant ideal, together with the corresponding prime of the base (proof lines 4273-4276).
Use surjectivity on the closed sets and the flatness assumption to find a prime of the target lying over it with flat local map (proof lines 4275-4278).
Choose a prime of the tensor product over both primes and identify the localised tensor product with a localisation of the tensor product of the local rings (proof lines 4279-4285).
Apply the flat base change criterion to conclude flatness of the module over the source local ring (proof lines 4286-4292).
proof_roadmap: Set up the primes and the flat local map (proof lines 4273-4278).
Move to the tensor product (proof lines 4279-4285).
Conclude by flat descent for a flat local base change (proof lines 4286-4292).
difficulty_reason: The lemma descends the flat-at-primes-over condition along an algebra map whose induced map on the closed sets defined by the two ideals is surjective and which is flat at the primes in question. The proof is a localisation chase: given a prime of the source lying over the ideal, surjectivity of the map on closed sets produces a prime of the target lying over it with a flat local map between the local rings, a prime of the tensor product is chosen over both, and the module becomes flat over the source after localising because it is flat after the flat base change, which is exactly the content of the flat-going-down lemma. The chain of localisations is spelled out.
